as_told.title: Analysis of the Roswell piece finds sub-wavelength waveguide channels

plain: Hal Puthoff, a physicist who has long worked on government-backed studies of unusual phenomena, says he examined a piece of layered bismuth and magnesium said to come from Roswell, the reported 1947 crash of a craft in New Mexico. He says he found it had tiny channels for guiding waves, a kind of part called a waveguide, far smaller than the waves themselves, which he calls quite an accomplishment. Podcast host Jesse Michels, relaying Puthoff, puts it as a claim that the material could shrink waveguides for terahertz frequencies, a band between radio and light; if true, it would point to deliberately engineered material beyond ordinary know-how.
